moments.title: Applications and matrix notation
moments.text: The presenter introduces matrices and mentions applications to transformations, probability and differential equations.

moments.title: Rows and columns
moments.text: Matrix order is written as number of rows by number of columns; the examples include $2\times2$ and $2\times3$ matrices.

moments.title: Addition and subtraction
moments.text: Matrices must have the same order, and corresponding entries are added or subtracted.

moments.title: Scalar multiplication
moments.text: Multiply each matrix entry by the scalar; the example multiplies matrix $A$ by 3.

moments.title: When is a matrix product defined?
moments.text: The number of columns of the first matrix must equal the number of rows of the second; the outer dimensions determine the result's order.

moments.title: Row by column
moments.text: For each entry of $AB$, combine a row of $A$ with a column of $B$ by multiplying matching entries and adding.

moments.title: Complete the product
moments.text: The video obtains $AB=\begin{pmatrix}16&6\\18&11\end{pmatrix}$ for its example.

moments.title: Determinant of a 2-by-2 matrix
moments.text: For the example $A=\begin{pmatrix}4&2\\5&3\end{pmatrix}$, $\det A=4(3)-2(5)=2$.

moments.title: Find the inverse
moments.text: The presenter applies the 2-by-2 inverse formula using the determinant, swaps the diagonal entries and changes the signs of the other two.

moments.title: Matrix terminology
moments.text: The video finishes with column, row, square, zero and identity matrices.

notes.title: When an inverse does not exist
notes.text: The example's determinant is nonzero, so its inverse exists. The video does not demonstrate the singular case.
notes.write: A square matrix is invertible exactly when its determinant is nonzero. If $\det A=0$, $A^{-1}$ does not exist.

moments.title: Using matrices for systems
moments.text: The video presents a matrix method for simultaneous equations. Matrix inverses are higher-level content; a calculator's simultaneous-equation solver also meets the SL technology requirement.

moments.title: Translate two orders into equations
moments.text: Let $c$ and $t$ be the prices of coffee and tea. The orders give $5c+3t=16.25$ and $2c+8t=15$.

moments.title: Write the system in matrix form
moments.text: The presenter arranges coefficients, unknowns and totals into $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$.

moments.title: From scalar algebra to matrices
moments.text: The presenter compares solving $3x=12$ with the matrix equation, then explains why a matrix inverse is used.

moments.title: Multiply by the inverse on the left
moments.text: Pre-multiplying both sides by $A^{-1}$ produces $A^{-1}A\mathbf{x}=A^{-1}\mathbf{b}$, provided $A$ is invertible.

moments.title: Use the identity matrix
moments.text: Since $A^{-1}A=I$ and $I\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{x}$, the solution is $\mathbf{x}=A^{-1}\mathbf{b}$.

moments.title: Apply the matrix method
moments.text: Use the coefficient matrix from the two orders and multiply its inverse by the column of totals.

moments.title: Evaluate the matrix expression
moments.text: The calculator gives $c=2.50$ and $t=1.25$; these values satisfy both original order equations.

moments.title: Extend the method
moments.text: The presenter explains that the same approach can be used with larger invertible coefficient matrices.

moments.title: Matrix tools on the calculator
moments.text: The presenter demonstrates matrix creation and operations on a TI-Nspire.

moments.title: Create a matrix
moments.text: A 2-by-2 matrix is entered and stored for later use.

moments.title: Arithmetic operations
moments.text: The stored matrix is reused for addition, subtraction, multiplication and a power.

moments.title: Determinant and inverse
moments.text: The video finds the determinant and then uses the inverse operation on the stored matrix.

moments.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
moments.text: The final portion moves to calculator commands for eigenvalues and eigenvectors, which connect to AHL 1.15.

moments.title: Interpreting an eigenvector
moments.text: The presenter notes that a calculator may return a different scalar multiple of an eigenvector.

moments.title: Continue practising
moments.text: The video recommends practising entry, storage and operations with matrices.

notes.title: Calculator shown
notes.text: This demonstration uses a TI-Nspire. Its menus and commands differ from the Casio fx-CG50.
notes.write: Use the correct matrix editor and operation commands for your calculator, and check dimensions and output.

ican.text: I can identify the order and entries of a matrix, and distinguish row, column, square, zero and identity matrices.
I can add and subtract matrices of the same order and multiply a matrix by a scalar.
I can determine whether a matrix product exists, find its order and calculate it by hand or with technology.
I can find a 2-by-2 determinant and inverse, and determine whether an inverse exists.
I can represent a system as $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ and solve it using an inverse or technology.
I can interpret matrix products in context and explain why multiplication order matters.

ku.text: An $m\times n$ matrix has $m$ rows and $n$ columns. Matrices can be added or subtracted only when their orders match; scalar multiplication acts on every entry.
If $A$ has order $m\times n$ and $B$ has order $n\times p$, $AB$ exists and has order $m\times p$. Each entry is a row-by-column sum.
Matrix multiplication is associative and distributive when the products are defined, but it is generally not commutative: $AB$ need not equal $BA$, and one product may be undefined.
The identity matrix satisfies $AI=IA=A$ when dimensions match. A zero matrix has every entry equal to zero.
A square matrix with zero determinant is singular and has no inverse. When $A$ is invertible, $A^{-1}A=AA^{-1}=I$.
For an invertible coefficient matrix, $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ has solution $\mathbf{x}=A^{-1}\mathbf{b}$. Matrix order matters: multiply the inverse on the left.

misc.better: The inner dimensions match, and the result uses the outer dimensions: $AB$ is $2\times4$.

misc.weak: Matrix multiplication means multiplying corresponding entries.
misc.better: Each entry of $AB$ is a row-by-column sum.
Matrix multiplication is generally not commutative; calculate both orders or use an appropriate counterexample.

misc.weak: A square matrix always has an inverse.
misc.better: Its determinant must be nonzero. A square matrix with determinant zero is singular.
Multiply by the inverse on the left: $\mathbf{x}=A^{-1}\mathbf{b}$.

terms.text: Check the inner dimensions, calculate row-by-column entries and report the resulting order.
Check that the determinant is nonzero; then apply the appropriate formula or technology and verify with the identity matrix.
Identify the unknown vector, write a consistent coefficient matrix and interpret the entries of the solution.

formula.text: For a $2\times2$ matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$, the booklet gives $\det A=ad-bc$ and $A^{-1}=\dfrac1{ad-bc}\begin{pmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}$ when $ad-bc\ne0$.

kq.q: Why must the inner dimensions match for a matrix product?
kq.model: Each entry pairs a row of the first matrix with a column of the second. These lists need the same number of entries to form the row-by-column sum.

kq.q: Why does a zero determinant prevent use of the 2-by-2 inverse formula?
kq.model: The formula divides by the determinant, so it is undefined when the determinant is zero. Such a matrix is singular and has no inverse.

kq.q: Why is an inverse multiplied on the left in $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$?
kq.model: The inverse is next to $A$ on the left: $A^{-1}A\mathbf{x}=I\mathbf{x}$. Matrix multiplication order cannot generally be reversed.

kq.q: What is the role of the identity matrix?
kq.model: It leaves a compatible matrix or vector unchanged under multiplication, analogous to multiplication by 1.
